messages:
ana: Heads-up: after the kernel-picker change landed in prod we see ~12% p50 host-side latency bump for short-chat traffic. attaching quick notes from a flame run.

mike: i noticed the p50 blip on the dashboard around 08:12 UTC. looked like ingress nodes, not GPU.

ana: quick numbers: host parse/tokenize p50 18ms -> 30ms, p95 45ms -> 68ms. total end-to-end still usually ok because batching masks it, but cold/small reqs are worse.

jordan: is this tokenization overhead, grpc framing, or proto unpack?

ana: flamegraph says parse_and_tokenize() + utf8_normalize is the hot path. allocation churn + a bunch of small writev syscalls. snippet from flame: parse -> normalize -> tokenize -> writev (many tiny iovecs).

sarah: did kernel-picker add extra prechecks? I thought the change only moved selection earlier.

ana: kernel-picker now runs a quick preflight heuristic that queries KV cache metadata to pick a compatible quantized kernel. that query ends up serializing proto header on the hot path for small requests -> extra memcpy + syscall.

eli: i can reproduce locally with the short-request harness. command i used: `./tools/harness --req samples/short_chat.json --profiling=flame`

mike: quick mitigation idea: gate the kvmeta query for requests under a token threshold (e.g., estimated_tokens < 64) so we skip the expensive proto serialize on small reqs.

ana: agreed. implemented local patch that skips kvmeta read for estimated_tokens < 64. testing now.

deploy-bot: @ana patch `skip-kvmeta-small-reqs` pushed to canary, build 4821 started.

jordan: also saw grpc writev explosion when chunking many tiny streaming frames. proxy ends up issuing many small writes which shows up as syscall tail time. we should coalesce small iovecs in the ingress proxy for streaming requests.

sarah: +1. and update batching heuristics to special-case single-frame streaming vs real streaming. single-frame streaming should avoid chunking.

ana: summarizing action items: 1) ana/mike -> temp-gate kvmeta query for small requests (PR in canary). 2) jordan/eli -> implement writev-coalesce in the ingress proxy and add tests. 3) sarah -> add a tokenization host-time metric to observability to track regressions. i'll open tickets.

mike: i'll run a 24h canary after the gate and post perf numbers here.

eli: repro logs (trimmed):
[2026-03-23T08:11:12Z] ingress-1 parse_and_tokenize: allocs=42 syscalls=18 writev_bytes=512 iovecs=9
[2026-03-23T08:11:12Z] ingress-1 post-kvmeta parse_and_tokenize: allocs=78 syscalls=34 writev_bytes=512 iovecs=21

ana: those logs line up with my flame. looks like the kvmeta path doubles small iovec count.

mike: ok moving fast on the gate, will report back. thanks team :thumbsup:

ana: thanks all — if anyone sees other regressions ping here or @eng-runtime.
